0.long_answer: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary cause of both laryngeal papillomatosis and cervical cancer. In the case of laryngeal papillomatosis, HPV types 6 and 11 are most frequently involved and lead to benign papillomatous growths in the larynx. For cervical cancer, high-risk types such as HPV 16 and HPV 18 are predominantly responsible, causing malignant transformations in cervical epithelial tissues. Overall, HPV is a group of viruses with different types causing varying clinical manifestations, but it remains the central viral etiology for these conditions.
